nodes.summary: Stand up the Python project root, environment, pytest runner, and application skeleton.
nodes.instructions:
Create the Python project root with pyproject.toml, a committed uv.lock, the .venv launchers
under bin/, and a pytest configuration so that `pytest -q` runs from the application root.

Create the app_server package with a create_app() factory returning a Flask app, and
app_server/testing.py exposing web_client(). Add tests/conftest.py exposing the web_client and
db_session fixtures. Do not create bin/test.sh here; the verification story owns it.
nodes.name: Stand up the Python project root, environment, pytest runner, and application skeleton.

acceptance.intent: The application factory returns a Flask application.
The published web_client callable yields a test client that answers an unregistered path with 404.
The project root carries the dependency manifest, lockfile, and test conftest.

nodes.summary: Reject a submission whose title is empty and report the reason.
nodes.instructions:
In the POST /books path, reject a missing, empty, or whitespace-only title with status 400 and
a non-empty reason. When the request sends Accept: application/json the body is JSON with
"error" (the reason) and "field" equal to "title"; otherwise the page is re-rendered with the
reason shown. Nothing is stored on rejection.
nodes.name: Reject a submission whose title is empty and report the reason.

acceptance.intent: An empty title on POST /books answers 400 with a non-empty reason naming the title field and stores nothing.
A whitespace-only title is treated as empty, rejected with 400, and nothing is stored.
A POST /books with no title field at all is rejected with 400 and nothing is stored.
A browser submission with an empty title is answered 400 with a re-rendered page and nothing is stored.
